newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas mixed, AECO eases on weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas mixed, AECO eases on weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were softer in Alberta but stronger at the export points, due to conflicting weather patterns, market sources said Thursday.
At the AECO storage hub, spot prices began as high as C$3.55 per gigajoule (GJ) but quickly softened to as low as C$3.31 late.
Traders said most deals for Friday delivery were done in the C$3.40-3.42 range, down four cents from Wednesday, as milder weather was forecast for Alberta on Friday.
February AECO prices were talked mostly around C$2.90 per GJ, easing by about 10 cents from Wednesday's level. Summer AECO traded in a wide range of C$1.66-1.75 per GJ.
At Sumas, Wash., prices ranged anywhere from $4.15 to $4.35 per million British thermal units (mmBtu). Most deals were reported done around $4.25, up about 14 cents on the day.
Storage fears in western Canada, where stocks were dipping below half capacity, continued to keep support in the export market, sources said.
Similarly at Niagara prices surged to the low-$5 per mmBtu area, leaping about 80 cents higher.
Sources attributed the sharp move to significantly colder temperatures forecast for the East on Friday and into this weekend.
However, gas stocks in the East as of January 3 were still well-above year-ago levels at 66.27 percent full. An updated Canadian Gas Association storage survey will be available early Friday.
